newsitem.title: USA: USDA expands crop insurance offerings to new areas.
newsitem.headline: USDA expands crop insurance offerings to new areas.

text.p: Wheat farmers in 25 additional states will be able to buy crop revenue coverage for their 1998 crop, the Federal Crop Insurance Corp said Friday.
Crop revenue coverage is a type of insurance that protects farmers against catastrophic drops in yields or prices.

FCIC also said its board of directors, in a meeting Thursday, voted to expand its offerings of Income Protection insurance for wheat and its canola pilot program. The board also approved pilot programs for almonds, pecans and sweet potatoes.
Crop revenue coverage is availabe in nine states now.

Beginning this fall, it will be available in the additional states of Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, New Mexico, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Carolina, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming.
FCIC chief Ken Ackerman said CRC would continue to be offered in Kansas, Michigan, Nebraska, South Dakota, Texas, Washington state, Minnesota and parts of North Dakota and Montana.
Income Protection polices protect farmers against reductions in gross income when prices or yields fall below a guaranteed level.
